messages:
nina: FYI I finished the bring-up bench + slice eval for kestrel-11b variants (int8 baseline, int6, int4-hybrid). posting the short summary and a proposed rollout for product/GTN.

harry: drop numbers plz, product wants a clear $$ vs quality tradeoff.

nina: numbers from mixed-production traffic sample (median prompt 48 tokens, mixed seq lengths):
- int8 (baseline): p50 120ms, p95 310ms, throughput 200 tok/s, unit cost $0.015/token-equivalent
- int6: p50 130ms, p95 340ms, throughput 235 tok/s, unit cost $0.0096/token-equivalent (~36% cheaper)
- int4-hybrid (KV+FP16 fallback for long context): p50 140ms, p95 420ms, throughput 270 tok/s for short queries, unit cost $0.0065/token-equivalent (~57% cheaper vs int8)
quality quick checks (GTN slices):
- short QA EM: int8 80.1%, int6 79.0% (delta -1.1), int4-hybrid 77.6% (delta -2.5)
- search snippet / rerank NDCG proxy: int8 0.72, int6 0.715 (-0.7%), int4-hybrid 0.701 (-2.4%)
- long summarize ROUGE proxy: int8 0.64, int6 0.61 (-4.7%), int4-hybrid 0.57 (-10.9%)
- hallucination proxy (contradiction flag): int8 3.8%, int6 4.2%, int4-hybrid 5.6%
sample sizes: ~8k queries total across 15 slices; longform slice smaller (1.2k) -> higher variance.

yosuke: int4-hybrid looks tempting for cost but the longform regression is big. is the hybrid fallback auto-triggered by token length?

nina: currently hybrid uses a quick heuristic: if prefix tokens > 512 or multi-turn depth > 3 -> route to float fallback (int6/int8) on the same model family. That explains the high p95 for int4-hybrid since fallback activates and we pay latency for two-stage handling on some requests. We can change policy to pre-route long contexts to int8 to avoid double-hop.

sara: product perspective : majority volume is snippet/rerank and we could save a lot. but enterprise longform customers will push back if quality drops. we need per-intent routing and clear GTN messaging.

harry: ops, any kernel/throughput constraints we should be aware of? p95 for int4-hybrid is concerning.

ops-bot: scheduled ticket created #KERNEL-4219 for int4 kernel warmup patch and batch tuning (owner: @yosuke). ETA 4d.

yosuke: quick note  the int4 kernels we used are experimental; reducing batch-size on long sequences and enabling our new fused-attn kernel cuts p95 by ~60-90ms in internal microbench. will test on canary.

nina: proposed routing + rollout (draft):
```
routes:
  - name: snippets-and-rerank
    match: intent in ["search_snippet","rerank","qa_short"]
    traffic_split: { int4-hybrid: 0.6, int6: 0.3, int8: 0.1 }
  - name: conversations
    match: intent in ["chat_multi_turn","assistant_shortform"]
    traffic_split: { int6: 0.8, int8: 0.2 }
  - name: longform
    match: intent in ["summarize_long","document_analysis"]
    traffic_split: { int8: 1.0 }
monitored_metrics: ["QA_EM","NDCG_proxy","ROUGE_proxy","hallucination_rate","latency_p95","cost_per_1k_tokens"]
rollback_rules:
  - if QA_EM drop > 1.5 pts absolute on any slice over 60m -> rollback affected slice to int8
  - if hallucination_rate increases > 1.0% absolute -> pause rollout
canary: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% over 24h windows, require stable metrics at each stage
```

sara: can you give GTN-friendly bullets? they want: net $ reduction, per-persona quality impact, recommended default, and comms language.

nina: GTN bullets draft: 
- expected unit cost reduction: int4-hybrid ~57% vs int8; int6 ~36% vs int8 (hosted pricing basis)
- persona impacts: search/rerank: quality impact small (<=2.5% NDCG delta int4-hybrid), short QA: mild EM delta (<=2.5 pts), longform: significant regression on int4-hybrid -> keep int8 for now
- recommendation: default to int6 for conversation features; enable int4-hybrid for high-volume snippet/rerank traffic with strict canary and per-slice QA_EM lower bounds; longform stays on int8 until kernel warmups and larger evals finish
- comms sample line: "We plan to optimize inference costs by introducing a low-precision serving tier for short-form/semantic search requests. This reduces token unit cost by up to ~57% for eligible traffic, with monitoring and automatic rollback to preserve quality for sensitive workloads."

harry: can you show $ savings example for a mid-market GTN customer (20M tokens/mo) and an enterprise heavy longform (120M tokens/mo with 40% longform)?

nina: quick math:
- 20M tokens/mo * (0.015 - 0.0065) = $170k/mo saved if all eligible traffic moves to int4-hybrid. realistic expected save ~50% of that -> $85k/mo.
- Enterprise: 120M tokens/mo, 40% longform -> eligible tokens = 72M. savings = 72M * (0.015 - 0.0065) = $612k/mo max. realistic ~60% of that = ~$367k/mo. numbers assume billed token-equivalent same across variants.

yosuke: action items: 1) ops to run two-day A/B (20k longform samples) to get variance; 2) kernel ticket #KERNEL-4219 priority P1; 3) nina to post GTN note and product summary; 4) sara to draft customer-facing FAQ and opt-out form.

sara: will draft comms and include opt-out for longform/enterprise customers.

ops-bot: canary deployment started for route "snippets-and-rerank" at 1688890288 -> 0.5% :rotating_light:

nina: thanks all  I'll upload the eval artifacts and per-slice CSVs to the shared drive and post the GTN note in 1h.
